What does the plan check cost?

With shared-out heights, 1.5–2.3% of flights wait about 40 s each at these densities. Against the filed plans that is 4.4× fewer delayed flights; in the high-return case (staff remark only), only 1.3× fewer. With this minimal check Amazon waits most (9–14% of its flights), mainly because it is the smallest fleet among two big ones: each conflict delays one flight, so the few Amazon flights carry a large share. With equal fleet sizes the gap shrinks by about 70% (FLEET). A smaller 2:1 lean against Amazon in its meetings with Wing remains; its cause is not tested.

What does the plan check cost?

With shared-out heights, 1–2% of flights wait about 35 s each at these densities (Houston 1.5–2.3%, about 40 s). Against the filed plans that is 4.1× fewer delayed flights (Houston 4.4×); in the high-return case (staff remark only), 1.6× fewer. With this minimal check Amazon waits most: 8.5% of its flights shared out, but 44% with the filed plans, because its 105 m return sits 4 m from Zipline’s 101 m cruise and it is the smallest fleet among two big ones (each conflict delays one flight). With equal fleet sizes the gap shrinks by about 70% (FLEET, Houston). Source: DFWPROC.

Does it hold at other traffic levels?

The headline uses the filed Houston site counts on one real layout, 10 runs (HEADLINE2). In the dense 12 km test patch the share removed by height sharing was 83% with sites every 4 km (30 runs), 80% at 3 km (15 runs) and 81% at 6 km (30 runs), counted 4 times a second (PRELAUNCH); an older once-per-second count gave 80% at 2 km (VALLOC). Planned conflicts grow roughly with the square of demand (exponent 1.65–1.7 in Houston, 2.3–2.4 in DFW; DENS1), so denser build-outs produce many more of them.

Does it hold at other traffic levels?

With DFW’s mix, the share removed by height sharing was 81% with sites every 2 km (95% range 79–83%) and 78% at 3 km (68–85%). At 4 km there are too few planned conflicts to tell (55%, range 11–79%); I had predicted at least 65% at every spacing, so that prediction failed. The real DFW layout at the filed site counts gives 80% over 10 runs (SEEDS). Source: DFWPROC.
